property.text: The coset_fft_field (SG-005) shift_factor MUST equal PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY. An incorrect shift factor would cause the coset to coincide with roots of vanishing polynomials, enabling division by zero in recover_polynomialcoeff.

reachability.notes: This is a constant correctness property. An incorrect PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY would be a fundamental implementation bug affecting all coset-based operations.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect shift factor causes systematic division-by-zero in all recovery operations, affecting every node running the incorrect implementation.

property.text: The bit-reversal permutation applied in polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007), coset_for_cell (SG-017), and coset_shift_for_cell (SG-016) MUST correctly map between evaluation-domain ordering and the canonical ordering expected by FFT. forall i: brp(brp(i)) == i (involution property).

reachability.notes: An incorrect bit-reversal permutation would produce wrong polynomial coefficients, leading to incorrect cells and proofs. This affects all blob processing and cell verification paths.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect permutation corrupts all polynomial conversions, producing incorrect proofs and cells that may or may not pass verification depending on the specific error.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a permutation implementation that produces incorrect polynomial coefficients.

property.text: In divide_polynomialcoeff (SG-010), the divisor polynomial b MUST NOT be the zero polynomial, and its leading coefficient b[bpos] MUST be nonzero. Division by zero polynomial MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: The divisor polynomial is the vanishing polynomial constructed from missing cell roots. If all cells are present (no missing roots), the vanishing polynomial is the constant 1, which is valid. However, edge cases in construction could produce a zero polynomial.

property.severity_justification: Division by zero polynomial crashes the node during proof generation or polynomial recovery.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing a set of missing cell indices that produces a zero vanishing polynomial.

property.text: In interpolate_polynomialcoeff (SG-011), all xs values MUST be distinct. forall i != j: xs[i] != xs[j]. Duplicate xs values would cause (xs[i] - xs[j]).inverse() to attempt inverting zero, resulting in a crash.

reachability.notes: The xs values are coset points derived from cell_indices. If duplicate cell_indices slip through validation, duplicate coset points would be passed to interpolation, causing a crash.

property.severity_justification: Division by zero in Lagrange interpolation crashes the validator node, causing single-node DoS.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing a crash in interpolation triggered by duplicate cell_indices that bypass validation.

property.text: In multiply_polynomialcoeff (SG-009), len(a) + len(b) MUST be <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB. This prevents the product polynomial from exceeding the extended evaluation domain, which would cause incorrect FFT results.

reachability.notes: The assertion prevents buffer overflow during polynomial multiplication. If many cells are missing (close to 50%), the vanishing polynomial can be large, and the product with another polynomial could exceed bounds.

property.severity_justification: Assertion bypass causes buffer overflow or incorrect polynomial arithmetic. Impact depends on memory safety of the implementation language.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating assertion bypass with specific missing cell patterns.

property.text: In coset_shift_for_cell (SG-016), cell_index MUST be in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). The assertion MUST be enforced before computing roots_brp[FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index].

reachability.notes: Attacker-controlled cell_index from P2P input. FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index could overflow or exceed array bounds.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds array access crashes the node or causes memory corruption.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing node crash from crafted cell_index.

property.text: In coset_for_cell (SG-017), cell_index MUST be in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB), and the returned Coset MUST have exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements. The slice roots_brp[start : start + FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL] MUST be in bounds.

reachability.notes: Same as PROP-0025 but for the full coset retrieval.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds slice access causes crashes or returns incorrect coset elements.

property.text: cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001) MUST produce a CosetEvals with exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements. Each cell byte segment [i*BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT : (i+1)*BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT] MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT bytes.

reachability.notes: Cells received via P2P are deserialized. If the cell is shorter than expected, byte slicing produces undersized field element bytes.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect field element count produces wrong coset evaluations, potentially causing verification errors.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC with malformed cell bytes.

property.text: coset_evals_to_cell (SG-002) is the exact inverse of cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001) for valid field elements. forall valid cell: coset_evals_to_cell(cell_to_coset_evals(cell)) == cell.

reachability.notes: Roundtrip property. If violated, recovered cells differ from originals even with correct polynomial.

property.severity_justification: Broken roundtrip causes recovered cells to differ from originals, producing invalid sidecars.

property.text: The _fft_field (SG-003) MUST require len(vals) to be a power of 2 and len(vals) == len(roots_of_unity). Non-power-of-2 inputs MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: FFT requires power-of-2 sizes for correctness. Non-power-of-2 sizes cause incorrect butterfly operations.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect FFT results propagate to all polynomial operations, producing wrong cells and proofs.
